events.title: Alexander defeats Darius III at Gaugamela
events.description: Alexander the Great routed the far larger army of the Persian king Darius III near Gaugamela in northern Mesopotamia. The victory broke Achaemenid power and opened the road to Babylon, Susa and Persepolis.

events.title: The Congress of Vienna is due to open formally
events.description: Europe's statesmen had gathered in Vienna to redraw the continent after Napoleon's fall, and 1 October was fixed for the Congress's formal opening. Its settlement shaped a balance of power that endured for decades.

events.title: John Philip Sousa takes charge of the US Marine Band
events.description: The 25-year-old John Philip Sousa became leader of the United States Marine Band. Over the next twelve years he turned it into a celebrated ensemble and began the career that earned him the name 'The March King'.
events.html: The 25-year-old John Philip Sousa became leader of the United States Marine Band. Over the next twelve years he turned it into a celebrated ensemble and began the career that earned him the name 'The March King'.

events.title: Congress creates Yosemite National Park
events.description: An Act of Congress established Yosemite National Park in California's Sierra Nevada, protecting the high country around the Yosemite Valley. John Muir's campaigning had helped make the case for preservation.
events.html: An Act of Congress established Yosemite National Park in California's Sierra Nevada, protecting the high country around the Yosemite Valley. John Muir's campaigning had helped make the case for preservation.

events.title: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China
events.description: From the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China. Communist victory in the civil war placed the world's most populous country under a new regime.
events.html: From the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China. Communist victory in the civil war placed the world's most populous country under a new regime.

events.title: 'In God We Trust' first appears on US paper money
events.description: The first US banknotes carrying 'In God We Trust', one-dollar silver certificates, entered circulation. Congress had made the phrase the national motto in 1956, at the height of Cold War anxieties about 'godless' communism.

events.title: Nigeria gains independence from Britain
events.description: Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, became independent from Britain with Abubakar Tafawa Balewa as prime minister. It was one of seventeen African states to win independence in 1960, the 'Year of Africa'.
